why: Controls below this project's own 28px coarse-pointer floor, recorded so the count cannot grow while the existing set is triaged. Not an allowance: every one of these is a real shortfall. Resizing them changes how the plugin feels and how nearly every capture looks, which is an operator decision rather than a repair one pass should make silently.
smallest: db-file-tag-remove at 10x14, db-multi-select-remove at 14x14, db-table-row-drag-handle at 16x16
note: db-toggle-switch measures 34x18 under a coarse pointer here, which is a second independent contradiction of roadmap 7.1's claim that the switch reaches 34x28.
lastTriage: 224 -> 228 on 2026-09-02, and the direction is not a regression. The invalid-events fixture had been drawing three rows and nothing else; it now draws what the modal builds — a per-row quick-fix button and the sticky action bar carrying Quick fix selected, Cancel and the destructive confirm. Those controls have always shipped at 24px on a phone (`db-invalid-event-row-fix` declares `height: 24px`, and the modal buttons inherit it), so what changed is that something finally measured them. Twelve controls in that one fixture now sit under the floor and four of them are net new to the count. They are real shortfalls of the same kind the 224 already holds, and they are recorded rather than resized for the reason stated above: the confirm button of a destructive modal is not a control to resize in the pass that first photographed it. Previously, 286 -> 224 on 2026-09-01. `db-list-row-open` (36) and `db-source-rule-icon-button` (26) were 2px short and had no coarse-pointer rule at all, so they were raised there rather than at the declaration — 26px is a density choice for the pointer that can hit it, and changing it at source would move every desktop capture to fix a phone. Raised with min-width/min-height, because the source-rule button declares its own min-width and a width alone loses to it.
